analysis.title: Global Economics Analyst: Macro Outlook 2027: Steady Baseline, Downside Risks
key_insights: Global GDP grew 2.7% in 2026, in line with potential and 0.1pp below GS's 2026 outlook projection. AI capex, easier financial conditions and fiscal expansion (US, Germany, parts of Asia) mostly offset the Iran-war energy supply shock.
Global headline inflation is on course to end 2026 at 3.7% Q4/Q4, 1.3pp above GS's forecast from last year, because of the Iran war.

GS forecasts 2027 global GDP growth of 2.8%, 0.1pp above potential. US 2.4% vs 2.2% consensus, Euro area 0.9% vs 1.3% consensus, China 4.5% vs 4.4% consensus, South Korea 3.2% vs 2.7%, Taiwan 6.3% vs 5.9%.

The energy impulse flips from a 0.4pp drag on global growth in 2026 to a modest boost in 2027. GS commodity strategists' baseline has Brent at $78/bbl by end-2027 with similar normalization in LNG prices. Europe keeps a drag from delayed energy cost pass-through.

GS FCI has tightened about 50bp in the US and 30bp in DMs over the last three months on lower equity prices and higher rates, implying a moderate growth drag over the next few quarters. The fiscal impulse is fading, with Japan the main exception (+0.7pp boost to GDP growth).

Global AI investment is forecast to rise from $1.1tn in 2026 to $1.8tn in 2027, driven by over $500bn more US hardware spending. The year-over-year change as a share of GDP peaks in 2027H1 and the level peaks in 2028. AI investment adds 0.4pp to global GDP growth, 0.2pp to measured US growth and 0.6pp to 'true' US growth after correcting for measurement bias.

China is a modest 0.1pp headwind to rest-of-world growth in 2027, with larger drags in Germany (-0.3pp) and Central Europe (-0.2pp). Chinese exports and the trade surplus stay strong while domestic demand is weak, with a 1.3pp of GDP property drag.

Risk 1, renewed energy shock: GS commodity strategists weight an upside scenario in which Iran escalation, shipping attacks and infrastructure damage push oil to $132/bbl. In that case the energy impulse stays a moderate drag on 2027 growth, and FCI and fiscal impulses would not offset it as they did in 2026.

Risk 2, bond market turbulence: the DM yield curve is 85bp above early 2026 levels. If sustained, that subtracts a cumulative 0.5% from GDP. Only part of this drag is in the baseline, because GS expects fewer central bank hikes than priced.

France is the acute fiscal risk: the 10-year OAT yield is about 150bp above Germany's. GS does not expect consolidation talks until after the April 2027 presidential and June parliamentary elections (it forecasts a 0.8pp deficit reduction in 2028), so the market could force an earlier consolidation.

Risk 3, weaker AI impulse: GS's baseline puts the shift to the second phase (lower hardware capex, more productivity gain and labor disruption) in 2028-2029, with US productivity trend at 2.5-3% and unemployment rising to 4.5%. Hyperscaler stock reactions to capex signals turned slightly negative in 2026 and upward capex revisions slowed in the Q3 earnings season.

Further AI capex risks: semiconductor and memory capacity constraints with order backlogs through 2028, credit markets (AI-related debt issuance of $687bn and equity issuance of $115bn so far in 2026, raising crowd-out risk), and regulation (possible data center permitting moratoria in several states, particularly Texas, after the US midterms).

Early signs of AI hitting the US labor market: across nonmanufacturing industries, firms' AI adoption now correlates significantly negatively with employment growth and significantly positively with unemployment. Correlations were insignificant at the start of the year. GS still sees the pressure as temporary, with a unemployment rise of about 0.5pp over several years, backloaded to 2028-2029.
US core PCE should slow from 3.2% at end-2026 to 2.4% at end-2027. Tariffs still add 40bp to y/y core PCE through October and should drop out of the y/y figures by next spring.

Near-term inflation risks: energy pass-through (especially Europe, e.g. airfares), rising memory prices, and broader upstream cost pressures. A January effect is expected in the US (a 0.1pp boost to January core PCE is in the forecast). GS sees most pressures as temporary, with wage growth trending down and shelter inflation softening.
In GS's adverse energy scenario, 2027 headline inflation runs 0.9pp above baseline and core 0.2pp above.

Fed: hikes expected in December and March, then one cut in December 2027 and three more in 2028 to a terminal rate of 3.25-3.5%. Scenario weights: 50% three hikes then cuts (baseline), 35% four hikes with a higher terminal rate, 15% recession. GS sees more dovish rate risk in the US than elsewhere because US inflation drivers look more temporary and the US is most exposed to an AI-cycle downturn.

ECB: final hike in December (another in Q1 possible), then normalization toward a 2.25% terminal rate starting 2027Q4. BoE: final hike to 4.25% in February, hold for the rest of 2027, cuts to 3.25% in 2028. BoC: two hikes to 3.0% in H1 2027. RBA: hold at 4.85% through October, with 125bp of cuts by end-2028. GS forecasts are dovish vs market pricing for the ECB and BoE.
BoJ is the outlier: another 25bp hike in December, then March and June hikes for a 2.0% terminal rate, with core CPI above 3.5% through next summer.
EM rates forecasts are dovish. Most CEEMEA and LatAm central banks are expected to cut through 2027. Asia is flat to slightly higher, and GS forecasts are below market pricing except in Taiwan.

Market baseline: positive returns in equities and bonds, near-zero returns in commodities. S&P 500 targets are 8300 (3m), 8500 (6m) and 8700 (12m) from 7619, and S&P 500 earnings growth is forecast to slow from 36% in 2026 to 11% in 2027. US equity gains should slow well below the 20%+ annualized pace of the last three years.

The AI capex peak is a bigger test for markets than for the economy. The AI impulse contributed far more to earnings and market value than to GDP, S&P 500 earnings are at a record high relative to GDP, and the second-derivative turn often matters even when growth stays healthy. AI infrastructure-levered stocks have de-rated significantly since June.

GS expects the baton to pass to other areas: hyperscalers if monetization becomes visible, AI-productivity beneficiaries, and non-AI companies as crowd-out eases. The risk is that the rotation away from recent winners becomes a bigger aggregate shock. GS sees market risk as higher than economic risk.

Bonds failed to hedge equities in 2026 because of the energy-driven inflation shock and a G10 hiking cycle, which pushed real rates sharply higher over the last 9 months. GS sees the risks shifting toward growth through 2027, which makes bonds a better hedge again. It sees the US 10-year yield at 4.6% at end-2027, from 4.99% now.

Allocation: overweight the US and Japan, neutral Asia ex-Japan/EM, underweight Europe. Credit spreads are expected to widen in 2027 on heavy corporate supply, with US HY expected to underperform. USD is forecast to weaken modestly, with CNY appreciating. A faster challenge to US tech exceptionalism would push USD lower, and JPY would appreciate in a growth-risk scenario.

Hedges GS flags: positioning for lower rates in the US and Japan, or for lower rates and equities together; USD/JPY downside; European gas futures and TTF calls for energy upside; and equity index volatility, which is unlikely to fall much and could rise if macro stresses broaden, with out-of-the-money puts or longer-dated calls replacing equity holdings.

sector_views.rationale: Earnings growth of 11% in 2027 and resilient AI investment support gains, though the pace slows.
Fiscal boost of 0.7pp to GDP growth and Topix target of 4500 at 12 months.
Tighter financial conditions and higher energy costs biting this winter keep GS growth at 0.9% vs 1.3% consensus.
Allocation is neutral, though GS targets rises in MSCI EM and MSCI AC Asia-Pac ex Japan.
Heavy corporate supply and AI-linked financing needs push spreads wider, with risk of turbulence in weaker borrowers.
Real yields are the highest in many years, bonds are regaining hedging value, and capital gains scope is higher later in 2027.
Baseline returns are near zero but commodities retain value as a hedge against energy shocks.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 earnings growth forecast to decelerate from 36% in 2026 to 11% in 2027 (GS forecast).
S&P 500 earnings are at a record high relative to GDP, and GS questions how much of the profit acceleration will persist as the AI investment cycle fades.
Hyperscaler equity reactions to earnings-call signals of higher capex turned slightly negative in 2026, and upward revisions to hyperscaler capex slowed in the Q3 earnings season.
Memory price forecasts were again revised higher during the last earnings season on robust demand.

trade_ideas.description: Long-dated equity index protection: out-of-the-money puts, or replace equity holdings with longer-dated call options
trade_ideas.rationale: Equity index volatility is unlikely to fall much and could rise as the cycle matures and macro stresses broaden.

trade_ideas.rationale: Protects against deeper downside growth tails, and bonds are regaining hedging value.
trade_ideas.risk: Fresh energy shocks or stickier core inflation could push yields higher.

risk_factors: Renewed Iran escalation causing another energy price surge (oil to $132/bbl in the adverse scenario).
Fiscal risk premium and bond market turbulence, especially in France, with large deficits and AI-linked borrowing pushing up long-term yields.
AI capex disappointment from capacity constraints, regulation, credit market stress or weaker demand.
Early AI-driven labor market weakness that could accelerate in a downside growth scenario.
Persistence of the record share of GDP going to US corporate earnings once the AI investment impulse fades.
Wider credit spreads on heavy corporate supply, with US HY the most exposed.
Stickier core inflation from memory prices, upstream costs and the January effect.
Tighter financial conditions in equities and rates as the main channel to a larger economic impact.
Black swan risks such as a major cybersecurity event.
vol_and_positioning: Equity index volatility has risen a little, is unlikely to fall much from here, and has scope to rise further if macro stresses broaden. The sharpest volatility so far has been under the surface of the major indices.
GS says longer-dated options can offer useful portfolio protection, via out-of-the-money puts or replacing equity holdings with longer-dated call options.

Positioning for lower rates in the US and Japan, or for jointly lower rates and equities, hedges deeper downside growth tails. USD/JPY downside plays a similar role because it performs well when rates and equities both fall.
European gas futures and TTF calls are described as asymmetric hedges against energy upside.

Significant derating of AI-infrastructure-levered companies since June. Volatility and rotations have mostly stayed under the surface of major equity and credit markets and could spill over to the index level.
geopolitical: War in Iran: renewed escalation could cause another energy price surge, with intensified shipping attacks and damage to oil infrastructure.
Oil risk premium has fallen coming into November, but a large and variable premium remains above fundamentals.
France fiscal concerns ahead of the April 2027 presidential election and June parliamentary election, with the OAT-Bund spread at about 150bp.

US midterm elections in early November raised the possibility of data center permitting moratoria in several states, particularly Texas. The Democratic victory in November's US election suggests some of the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act spending cuts will be reversed.
Japan: Takaichi administration's investment plans, consumption tax cuts and higher defense spending.
US tariff pass-through is ending, with the boost to core PCE to fully drop out by next spring.
Trade uncertainty looms over the Bank of Canada outlook.

tension_points.bull_case: AI investment still rises to $1.8tn in 2027 and S&P 500 earnings grow 11%, which cushions the transition, and the baton may pass to hyperscalers, AI-productivity beneficiaries and non-AI companies.
tension_points.bear_case: Hyperscaler stock reactions to capex have turned negative, upward capex revisions are slowing, and the record share of GDP going to US earnings may not persist. Capacity constraints, credit stress or regulation could disappoint, and the passing of the baton may not be smooth.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sharper reversal in the AI boom or earlier AI-related labor market disruption, or the market looking ahead to the 2028 peak in the investment share.

tension_points.bull_case: Brent normalizes to $78/bbl by end-2027, turning the energy impulse into a modest growth tailwind, and faster progress toward resolution would help equities and bonds.
tension_points.bear_case: Escalation could push oil to $132/bbl, keeping a drag on growth and adding 0.9pp to headline inflation, with FCI and fiscal impulses no longer offsetting it.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Intensified shipping attacks, damage to oil infrastructure, and a more persistent risk premium.

tension_points.bull_case: Central banks deliver fewer hikes than priced, so forward rates fall and the US 10-year reaches 4.6% by end-2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Large deficits and heavy AI-linked borrowing could push long yields up more sharply, especially in France, subtracting 0.5% from GDP if the DM curve stays 85bp higher.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The French market forcing earlier fiscal consolidation ahead of the April and June 2027 elections.
